title: Reverse Linked List II
summary: Reverse the order of the existing nodes from position left through position right in a singly linked list and return its new head.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–500 nodes with values in [−500,500]. 1 ≤ left ≤ right ≤ node count. Fixtures serialize the next chain as a value array. The validator also checks node identities, links, unchanged node values, and termination.
contractDetails.output-checking: Build an acyclic ListNode chain. Invoke reverseBetween(head,left,right). Verify the complete expected sequence of original node identities and unchanged node values, reject clones, extra nodes and cycles, then serialize values.

statement: Reverse the order of the existing nodes from position left through position right in a singly linked list and return its new head. Positions here are one-based. Keep all other nodes in their original relative order. Relink the existing nodes without changing their values.

examples.explanation: Only positions two through four reverse.
Even equal-valued nodes must move to the correct identity positions.
Reversing a one-node interval preserves the node.

constraints: 1–500 nodes with values in [−500,500]. 1 ≤ left ≤ right ≤ node count. Fixtures serialize the next chain as a value array. The validator also checks node identities, links, unchanged node values, and termination.
hints: Conceptual: Only the links around and within one interval need to change.
Directional: Use a temporary predecessor before the head so the interval may start at position one.
Implementation: Repeatedly detach the node after the interval’s first node and move it immediately after the predecessor.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary solution space. The identity-checking wrapper uses O(n) audit storage.
